newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Goh decries need for multiparty system.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Goh decries need for multiparty system.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, expected to call general elections soon, has said the tiny country could not have achieved what it has under a multi-party system.
"Do you think we could have done even half of what was achieved in the last 30 years if we had a multi-party system and a revolving door government?" he asked students on Friday evening.
"Do you think we could have done just as well if we had a government which was constantly being held in check by 10 to 20 opposition members in the last 30 years?" he asked.
In the parliament dissolved on Monday, opposition parties held just four of the 81 elected seats in parliament.
They frequently complain that Goh's People's Action Party (PAP), which has won every election since 1959, makes sure the election scales are heavily weighted in its favour.
Goh began his speech to students at the Nanyang Technological University by describing Singapore 30 years ago, when unemployment was around 14 percent and prospects were uncertain.
Now, he said, Fortune Magazine placed Singapore third behind Toronto and London on the list of the world's best cities to live in.
Singapore's per capita Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is now bigger than that in Britain, the former colonial power.
The next elections, which the PAP is expected to win in another landslide, are widely forecast for early January.
